subject: I
fact: I realized I had crossed a threshold I didn't notice crossing, and felt bigger, more there.
source_quote: Something hit me, as I surveyed the battlefield. Not literally. Though, given how the last several months have gone, that's worth specifying. No, this was the other kind of thing — the quiet knock inside the chest that means you've crossed some threshold you didn't notice crossing. I've felt it before, in the dark, after bad fights. The body takes stock before the mind does. I was bigger somehow. More there.

subject: I
fact: I heard myself think that we were all leveled up before I fully understood it.
source_quote: "Alright, so the first thing is that we're all leveled up." I heard myself think it before I quite understood it. Leveled up.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz made a noise of genuine surprise and declared that we're gonna level up.
source_quote: Daz made a noise of genuine surprise — the kind he usually reserves for things like demon princes and sentient oozes. "Oh!" And then, with that particular tone he uses when he's already processed something and moved to judgment: "We're gonna level up."

subject: I
fact: I take seriously the question of what kind of fighter I am becoming, and that takes time.
source_quote: I knew immediately how long that was going to take. Not because I couldn't decide, but because I take it seriously, and taking things seriously takes time.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir finds it more fun to double down with an obscure specialization and then try to break the universe with it.
source_quote: "I find it more fun to double down with some sort of obscure specialization and then try to break the universe with it."

subject: I
fact: I realized that being a dwarf raised by giants means I don't have to have any range, because giants toss rocks.
source_quote: "See," I thought, "being a dwarf raised by giants means I don’t have to have any range. Giants toss rocks. Those rocks go far and hurt. My job was to be there and protect the giants from anything that came too close."

subject: Our lack of ranged weapons
fact: We have no ranged weapons, and this will come back and bite us in a dangerous world where distance matters.
source_quote: The Underdark is tight and low. But we're almost out. And this is a dangerous world, and we have a dangerous job, and we none of us have ranged weapons, which means there will absolutely be something that needs hitting from a distance. The universe is that kind of petty.

subject: I
fact: I confirmed that Dawnbringer deals Radiant damage, not slashing, and burns rather than cuts.
source_quote: "So question, so Dawnbringer is not slashing, right? It's actually… Radiant damage." Confirmed. The blade doesn't cut so much as it burns — clean, divine, the kind of light that argues with darkness on a philosophical level.

subject: I
fact: I have a habit of saving potions for later, even though I know it's wrong.
source_quote: "Okay, so I'm the type, when I adventure, I'm always like, oh, I don't know, I'm gonna save this potion for later, I might need it." I knew it was wrong when I said it. It's always wrong. The potion you don't drink is the potion you die holding.

subject: My potion-saving habit
fact: I have a bad habit of saving potions for later, and I recognize it as one more habit to account for.
source_quote: Which — I recognized, even as I thought it — had given me one more bad habit to account for.

subject: I
fact: I am considering adopting Zhentarim Tactics — ruthless, efficient, uncomfortable — because I’ve absorbed lessons from the Underdark.
source_quote: "Zhentarim Tactics." The Zhentarim are not good people. I know that. The hill giants weren't always good people either, and I carry their lessons in the shape of every fight I've won. I've had what you might call a dark transition.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognized that adopting Zhentarim Tactics would be a whole change of character for me.
source_quote: "That would be a whole change of character for you."

subject: I
fact: I acknowledged I could work Zhentarim Tactics into my story, even if it wasn't the honesty I preferred.
source_quote: "Well, I mean, I can work it into my story." I could. It would be honest, even. Not the honesty I prefer — I've always liked honesty you can stand behind without flinching — but there are things you absorb down here whether you mean to or not.

subject: I
fact: I understood that the Underdark doesn't care what kind of person you want to be.
source_quote: The happy-go-lucky kid who went underground expecting something survivable has spent months watching demon lords and eating mushrooms and coming to understand that the Underdark doesn't care what kind of person you want to be.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt pleasure in the moment before decision, when possibilities are laid out like a hand of cards.
source_quote: There is a particular kind of pleasure in having options. Not the pleasure of having made the decision — that comes later, and sometimes not at all. The pleasure I mean is the one that arrives in the moment before: the spread of possibilities laid out like a hand of cards, each one representing a different version of how the next fight might go.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Warcaster improves concentration checks, which is vital for maintaining spells like Hypnotic Pattern.
source_quote: Warcaster was the obvious answer, and I noted it without sentiment. If I'm maintaining concentration on a spell worth maintaining — Hypnotic Pattern, Maximilian's Grasp — then the ability to hold that concentration when something lands a hit is not decorative. It is the difference between the spell persisting and the spell dissolving at precisely the wrong moment.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considered Fey Touched because it grants two additional prepared spells and free castings.
source_quote: Fey Touched gives me two additional spells to prepare. Plus free castings.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized that free Misty Step allows escape without attacks of opportunity and from grapples.
source_quote: No — being able to cast it without expending a spell slot is extremely useful. Because if you're in combat, it allows you to get out without incurring attacks of opportunity. It allows you to get out of a grappled situation.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considered Telekinetic as a geometry tool to reposition allies, not just enemies.
source_quote: Telekinetic, I can aim this at allies and do things like get them out of a grapple. Move them five feet.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized that his spell selection, Warcaster, Misty Step, and Sculpt Spells form an interlocking system of battlefield control.
source_quote: The idea was forming as I spoke it. Sculpt Spells lets me carve exclusions into area effects. But the area effects I could now access, combined with the concentration durability Warcaster would provide, combined with the escape utility of free Misty Step — these were not independent features. They were a system.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood that the fight before the fight — positioning and preparation — is most of the fight.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel had a chapter about this. He called it "the long arrangement" — the idea that the fight before the fight, the positioning, the preparation, is actually most of the fight.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz identified Street Justice as a feat that lets Zalthir bind enemies he's already grappled.
source_quote: I found the Street Justice feat on his behalf — the one that let him use rope to bind enemies he'd already grappled.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognized that a grapple fixes a target in place, making Cloud of Daggers more effective.
source_quote: If you hold one in place," Daz said, "the daggers keep finding them." I had been thinking about it too. Cloud of Daggers: a rotating cage of blades, hungry in one fixed point in space. The problem has always been that enemies move. But a grapple — a proper hold, weight-to-weight, the kind that pins something to a specific square of floor — that solved it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir confirmed that he can grapple a target without being inside the Cloud of Daggers, so he won't take damage from it.
source_quote: A grapple keeps the target where I put them, but I am not inside them — I am beside them, adjacent, occupying my own space while they occupy theirs. Daz could put his cloud directly on the grappled target and I would walk away without a scratch.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted that grapple is a quick action, but binding with rope consumes a full turn.
source_quote: Grapple is a quick thing — one motion, a grab, a test of weight and leverage, done in the space of a heartbeat. That leaves the hands. Rope is slower. Tying something takes focus, takes both hands, takes the better part of a turn spent crouching over a target that is probably trying to bite you.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized that a full turn spent grappling and binding an enemy leaves him free to act next turn while the enemy remains pinned and damaged.
source_quote: The whole turn — both pieces of it — spent on one enemy, pinned to the floor, with Daz's daggers already spinning above them. That was a full turn spent on setup. The next turn, I would be free — and whatever I had tied down would still be there, still bleeding, while I moved to the next problem.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled a monastery lesson on battlefield geometry but couldn't remember the details.
source_quote: I said: there was a class on this. At the monastery. Something about battlefield geometry and the difference between control and proximity. I think it was Brother Heslin — or possibly that was the one who taught falling. I'm genuinely uncertain. Either way, I remember the light through the shuttered window and thinking the form was taking too long. I did not remember what they said.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is quiet and deliberate, preferring to acknowledge complexity without complaint.
source_quote: He said very little, which is Zalthir's preferred mode. Just: "Feats, huh." And then, with the considered weight of someone who was not actually complaining but acknowledging a genuine complexity: "Yeah, this'll take some time."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz wrote down Fey Touched with quiet satisfaction after confirming it was the optimal choice.
source_quote: Fey Touched. That was the one. I wrote it down with the quiet satisfaction of a calculation that checks out.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum made a sound.
source_quote: Grygum made a sound.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin said something about 'the Ember Grapple.'
source_quote: Thorin said something about 'the Ember Grapple.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Someone — possibly Thorin again, possibly Grygum, it is hard to tell when they are both making noise — found this very funny.
source_quote: Someone — possibly Thorin again, possibly Grygum, it is hard to tell when they are both making noise — found this very funny.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin mentioned javelins.
source_quote: Thorin mentioned javelins.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin had apparently acquired some facility with thrown weapons — a Sharpshooter's instinct, trained in, applied to range — and he wanted something with reach for the next engagement.
source_quote: Thorin had apparently acquired some facility with thrown weapons — a Sharpshooter's instinct, trained in, applied to range — and he wanted something with reach for the next engagement.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted something to hold the gap while I was busy tying knots and Daz was busy making things into fire.
source_quote: Thorin wanted something to hold the gap while I was busy tying knots and Daz was busy making things into fire.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin found the situation practical.
source_quote: Practical. I noted it and moved on.

subject: Narrator
fact: I had run the tunnels in my head — the distance we had traveled, the pace, the absence of obvious threats immediately ahead.
source_quote: I had run the tunnels in my head — the distance we had traveled, the pace, the absence of obvious threats immediately ahead.

subject: Narrator
fact: I had turned that over the way I turn most things over: once, completely, and then I put it down.
source_quote: I turned that over the way I turn most things over: once, completely, and then I put it down.

subject: Narrator
fact: The math was the math.
source_quote: The math was the math.

subject: Narrator
fact: What we had was what we had.
source_quote: What we had was what we had.

subject: The Ember Grapple
fact: The Ember Grapple holds something still until there is nothing left to hold.
source_quote: The Ember Grapple holds something still until there is nothing left to hold.

subject: The Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard charges in with fire and flash and the announcement of itself.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard charges in with fire and flash and the announcement of itself.

subject: The Ember Grapple
fact: The Ember Grapple is a name that has been accepted, though its origin or exact referent remains ambiguous.
source_quote: I let it settle. As names go, I have heard worse.

subject: The Ember Grapple
fact: The Ember Grapple may describe the same party as the Ember Vanguard, but from a different position in the room — this is not confirmed.
source_quote: Both accurate. Possibly the same party described from two different positions in the room.
